correctness.rationale: In a fixed (A,B,C) binary Parikh fiber, if one word has subsequence-universality index >=2 then A,B>=2 and 0<C<AB, ensuring every member has index>=2. The greedy arch characterization and two-symbol-per-arch length constraint preclude any spectrum hole through length seven; at length eight an index-four word is exactly four blocks each ab or ba, forcing A=B=4 and C=6+t for t in 0..4. Explicit index-three words fill the would-be hole for C=6,7,9,10. For C=8, all nonnegative x_0..x_4 with sum 4 and weighted sum 8 correspond bijectively to the eight partitions of 8 fitting in 4x4: two have exactly two arches, the other six four arches, yielding exactly {2,4}. A new independent exhaustive implementation tested every binary subsequence pattern for all 511 words of lengths 0..8, found 255 actual fibers, verified greedy arch indices separately, and recovered just that one eight-word noninterval fiber.
residual_risks: Statement is only the first occurrence and uniqueness through length eight; no all-length spectrum classification.
Finite exhaustive classification is justified by the independent all-length structural cutoff argument, not by extrapolating 511 samples.
